I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I have $772 and am on CHANCE. My pink and orange monopolies are heavily built. p2 has cash of $345 and owns red properties at 3/3/4 with Boardwalk unmortgaged. p3 is bankrupt.

p4 has $16 and owns yellows with houses. The bank has 3 houses and 12 hotels left. NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE is unowned.

The bank now has 3 houses remaining. I can build on ST_CHARLES, STATES, and ST_JAMES. Virginia cannot be built on because the pink monopoly requires even distribution.

Building one house on St James for $100 will complete the orange monopoly at 4/4/4. This raises rent to $800 and delivers a kill shot.

I am weighing whether to split the remaining two houses between St Charles and States for $200, or to build evenly on all three pink properties. I am also double-checking the exact rent values for each house level.

I am correcting the rent values for this game variant. Standard US Monopoly orange rent is $750 for Tennessee at four houses and $875 for New York at four houses. The earlier figures of $750/$800 were approximate or from a different edition.

I am cross-referencing the rent figures against earlier turns. p4 paid exactly $550 for St James with three houses. I am also checking p2's red properties: Kentucky and Indiana at four houses should be $875 each, while Illinois at four houses is likely $1100 in standard US Monopoly.

I am treating this as standard US Monopoly because the $550 St James rent matches the standard three-house tier. Tennessee and New York are not listed as buildable because they already have four houses, so only hotels remain possible there. Virginia is also excluded from building since it is at two houses.

The sellable building spaces are Virginia, Tennessee, and New York. Virginia is the highest on the pink monopoly. Tennessee and New York are the highest on the orange monopoly. This confirms the even-building rule prevents selling from St Charles, States, or St James first.

The orange rent jump from $550 to $750 is the most critical landing on that street. I am now comparing three options: building one house on St James and one each on St Charles and States for $300, leaving $472; building only St James for $100, leaving $672; or attempting to build pink to 3/3/3.

Building pink to 3/3/3 is impossible with only three houses remaining. The current two-house rent on St Charles and States is $50 each, so raising them to two would add only $100 in rent. p4 has just paid $550 in rent and now has only $16.

p4 can liquidate roughly $730 from houses and mortgages. That is more than enough to survive a single large rent. They are not instantly bankrupt.

p4's liquidation is now roughly $746. St James at four houses would charge $750, which could bankrupt them.

St James at four houses would bankrupt p4 by exactly four dollars. The current three-house rent leaves them with $196, so adding the fourth house is essential to guarantee a kill. p2's red properties are also being liquidated; selling all ten houses there yields $750.

p2's liquidation is roughly $1,295. Even a New York hotel at $1,100 would not bankrupt them. Hotels are therefore ineffective against p2. The bank has only three houses left, so building three houses would leave the bank with no houses.

Hotel upgrades return four houses to the bank. If I build a hotel on St James, p2 could immediately buy two more houses and reach four on the reds for $300. That would raise red rent to $875 each.

I am now calculating my own liquidation. If I land on a red with four houses, I can sell orange and pink houses for roughly $800, plus cash, to survive. Building only the St James house leaves me with $672 in cash plus that same $800 in sellable assets. That is enough to survive a red four-house hit. Hotels are too dangerous because they return four houses to the bank, which would let p2 reach four houses on the reds immediately. I will not build a hotel. The single St James house costs $100 and leaves the bank with two houses.

p4 cannot build on the yellows. They only have $16 cash and each house costs $150. p2 can buy two houses from the bank to reach four on the reds. That would raise red rent to $875 each. I must consume the remaining bank houses to block that.

I will buy all three remaining houses to empty the bank and lock out p2. This prevents them from reaching four houses on the reds.

I will build one house each on St James, St Charles, and States for $300. This leaves the bank with zero houses and locks out p2 from reaching four houses on the reds. The remaining cash is $472.

I am now checking p2's position on the board to see which properties they can land on next. p2 is currently on Pennsylvania Railroad.

p2's next rolls from Pennsylvania Railroad will hit St James, Tennessee, and New York. All three are my orange properties. The other possible lands are their own reds, the yellows, and Community Chest.

p2 has an 8/36 chance of landing on my orange properties next turn. Even a single four-house hit would force them to sell eight houses from their red monopoly. That would cripple their housing stock and secure the win.

p4 is on St James and will roll away next turn. p2 can land on Tennessee or New York from there. The current turn index is 105, so this is my post-turn action after resolving the Chance card.

I am now checking whether p2 could land on my orange properties before p4 moves. If p2 sells houses to pay rent, those houses return to the bank. p4 cannot afford them with only $16 cash, so p2 would have to rebuy them later. This confirms the housing lock remains intact.

p4 has a 7/36 chance of landing on Tennessee or New York from St James. Those streets are already four houses, so p4 would still be bankrupted even without upgrading St James.

I am now weighing whether to unmortgage any of my properties. The costs to unmortgage Baltic, Vermont, Connecticut, and Short Line range from $33 to $110.

Unmortgaging is not worthwhile. No light blue or dark purple monopolies exist, so the rent gain is negligible. The Short Line is only worth $25, not $110. Trading with p2 and p4 would require giving up Boardwalk for Park Place, which is too expensive and unlikely to succeed.

I will not trade. No beneficial deals exist. Selling orange or pink properties would be suicidal. The Get Out of Jail Free card is too valuable to give up. I will not offer cash to p4 because that would help them survive. I will reject any trade proposals that could hurt my position.

I will build one house on St James, St Charles, and States now. I can only make one tool call, so I will not propose a trade. The engine might apply the trade immediately and ask again, but building is the clear positive expected value.

Tennessee and New York cannot be upgraded to hotels right now because they are not in the buildable space keys. Hotels would return four houses to the bank, so I will not build them.
